answer: A borescope's narrow horizon shows a hairline crack only when the blade is rotated past the probe under controlled light, so each AI agent identity must be bound to a rotating hardware attestation key that signs every action, making cloned identities fail verification. Like juniper inspecting each fan blade at a fixed index, the registry maps one key to one agent and flags any second key claiming the same identity. This terrace of signed checkpoints costs an attacker a fresh physical root per sybil, but cannot stop compromised genuine hardware.
